Product Specification Case Study
Example product: Women's relaxed-fit cotton T-shirt.
Example product color: Black.
Example product sizes: S/M/L/XL.
Example seller SKU `FSH-TEE-001`.
Column labels: Stage / What Happens
Stage Intake: seller provides the product input fields.
Intake input provided by seller: SKU.
Intake input provided by seller: product images.
Intake input provided by seller: product name.
Intake input provided by seller: brand.
Intake input provided by seller: fabric composition.
Intake input provided by seller: colors.
Intake input provided by seller: sizes.
Intake input provided by seller: MRP.
Intake input provided by seller: care instructions.
Intake input provided by seller: size chart.
Stage Understand: agent identifies a women's T-shirt.
Stage Understand: agent identifies black color.
Stage Understand: agent identifies relaxed fit.
Stage Understand: agent identifies cotton composition.
Stage Understand: agent identifies four sizes.
Stage Classify: agent maps the product to the appropriate apparel/T-shirt category for each selected marketplace.
Stage Extract: agent normalizes 'Jet Black' to the marketplace's accepted black value where appropriate.
Extract stage preserves the seller-provided value while normalizing to the marketplace value.
Stage Canonical: one product record is built for the product.
Canonical product record contains identity.
Canonical product record contains attributes.
Canonical product record contains variants.
Canonical product record contains media.
Canonical product record contains compliance.
Canonical product record contains content.
Stage Generate: agent creates title.
Stage Generate: agent creates bullets.
Stage Generate: agent creates description.
Stage Generate: agent creates relevant keywords.
Generated content uses only verified facts.
Stage Validate: checks all marketplace-specific mandatory/conditional fields.
Stage Validate: checks variant/media rules.
Stage Human: if a marketplace requires a missing fabric detail, the agent asks one targeted question.
Stage Submit: agent submits the marketplace-specific representation.
Stage Error: marketplace rejects one size because the size value is invalid.
On size rejection the agent maps the canonical size to the accepted marketplace value.
After mapping the corrected value, the agent revalidates.
Stage Resubmit: corrected listing is submitted.
Stage Live: marketplace confirms the listing active.
Marketplace Listing ID is stored on LIVE.
Marketplace listing URL is stored on LIVE.
Stage Dashboard: product shows LIVE for that marketplace.
Dashboard shows separate statuses for any other marketplaces still processing.

§22 V1 Acceptance Criteria
V1 acceptance: a seller can create a brand profile once.
V1 acceptance: the brand profile is reused across products.
V1 acceptance: a seller can provide apparel product information through a structured form.
V1 acceptance: a seller can provide apparel product information through bulk input.
V1 acceptance: the system can represent one style with multiple color/size variants.
V1 acceptance: every important canonical attribute can retain its source.
V1 acceptance: every important canonical attribute can retain its confidence.
V1 acceptance: the system can map one canonical product into marketplace-specific category/field structures.
V1 acceptance: the system can distinguish required, conditional, optional and unsupported fields.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate title.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate bullets.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate description.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate keywords.
V1 acceptance: title, bullets, description and keywords are generated from verified product facts.
V1 acceptance: the system can validate the product before submission.
V1 acceptance: the system can show blocking reasons.
V1 acceptance: the system can identify missing data.
V1 acceptance: the system can ask targeted human questions.
V1 acceptance: the system can submit a listing.
V1 acceptance: the system records the submission attempt.
V1 acceptance: the system can read the resulting marketplace status/error.
V1 acceptance: the system can automatically fix defined deterministic error classes.
V1 acceptance: the system can retry safely without creating uncontrolled duplicate submissions.
V1 acceptance: the system can escalate unresolved issues to a human.
V1 acceptance: the system confirms a listing as LIVE only after marketplace success confirmation.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show per-marketplace status.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show listing identifiers.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show issues.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show latest activity.
V1 acceptance: the system preserves history so the team can understand what changed and why.
§23 Product Metrics for V1
Column labels: Metric / Definition
V1 metric "Time to first listing": time from complete product intake to first successful live listing.
V1 metric "Listing success rate": percentage of listing jobs that reach LIVE without manual marketplace intervention.
V1 metric "First-pass success rate": percentage of submissions accepted without a correction cycle.
V1 metric "Auto-resolution rate": percentage of errors resolved by the agent without seller intervention.
V1 metric "Human question rate": percentage of products requiring at least one seller question.
V1 metric "Average human questions per SKU": questions asked per product/job.
V1 metric "Error recurrence rate": percentage of issues that reappear after correction.
V1 metric "Duplicate submission rate": unwanted duplicate listing/submission incidents.
V1 metric "Attribute completeness": percentage of required/conditional fields correctly populated before submission.
V1 metric "Live confirmation accuracy": percentage of listings marked LIVE that are actually live.
§24 Handoff to Lead Engineer: these items must be clear before build.
Canonical product is the source of truth.
Marketplace listings are derived representations of the canonical product.
Marketplace schemas are versioned.
Marketplace schemas can change.
Every field should have a source.
Critical facts should have confidence/evidence.
Required fields are marketplace + category + context dependent.
Variant relationships are first-class product data, not just a UI feature.
Listing status is per marketplace.
Listing status is per variant where necessary.
Errors are first-class records.
Error records carry classification.
Error records carry severity.
Error records carry resolution state.
Human questions are first-class workflow tasks, not generic support tickets.
Every submission should be auditable.
Every correction should be auditable.
The workflow must be resumable.
If a seller answers one question, the agent continues from the blocked step rather than restarting the entire job.
The agent must be idempotent at the business level.
Repeated status checks or safe retries should not create duplicate product identities.
The system should preserve marketplace-specific data.
The canonical product must not be polluted with marketplace-only fields.
§25 Open Product Decisions must be locked before implementation.
Column labels: Decision / Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss
Open decision 'Exact marketplace launch order', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: pick 2–3 marketplaces for first production validation.
Open decision 'Exact marketplace launch order', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: add adapters incrementally.
Open decision 'Seller input method', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: start with guided form + spreadsheet upload.
Open decision 'Seller input method', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: add connected PIM/ERP after core workflow is stable.
Open decision 'Human approval', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: default to autonomous submission after validation.
Open decision 'Human approval', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: optional approval mode for cautious sellers.
Open decision 'Content language', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: start with English.
Open decision 'Content language', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: keep the content model language-ready.
Open decision 'Image generation', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: do not make image generation a dependency for V1 listing completion.
Open decision 'Marketplace schema refresh', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: treat schema/rules as versioned and refreshable rather than static.
Open decision 'Error library', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: build an internal error taxonomy.
Open decision 'Error library', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: continuously map marketplace errors into the internal error taxonomy.
Open decision 'Confidence threshold', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: define which attributes can be inferred and which always require evidence/confirmation.
Open decision 'Bulk listing', Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss: design for one SKU and bulk SKU jobs from the same underlying workflow.

Executive Summary & Timeline
The plan is an aggressive, production-ready roadmap to build and launch an AI-powered marketplace listing operator for D2C brands.
Launch marketplaces: Amazon and Flipkart.
Foundational architecture is built solo for ~10 days.
Then 4 engineers are onboarded (5-person team total).
Sprint Duration: 45 Calendar Days.
Sprint dates: Mon Sep 21, 2026 → Wed Nov 4, 2026.
Team Model: 1 Solo → 5 People.
10-day foundation sprint.
Then 35 days scaled.
Cloud Platform: Google Cloud (GCP).
Cloud platform component: Cloud Run.
Cloud platform component: Cloud SQL pgvector.
Cloud platform component: Redis.
Cloud platform component: KMS.
Launch Scope: Amazon + Flipkart.
Amazon adapter uses LWA SP-API.
Flipkart adapter uses Flipkart Seller API.
Day-45 Definition of Done
On Day 45, a real D2C brand user must complete the full journey end-to-end in production without any manual engineering intervention.
DoD: user signs in securely via JWT.
DoD: user selects a brand.
DoD: maintain 100% tenant-scoped data isolation.
DoD: connect an Amazon and/or Flipkart account via OAuth.
DoD: marketplace credentials encrypted at rest.
DoD: import products via CSV (bulk).
DoD: import products via manual entry.
DoD: product import has automated validation.
DoD: image upload to GCS.
DoD: trigger AI generation for title.
DoD: trigger AI generation for bullets.
DoD: trigger AI generation for description.
DoD: trigger AI generation for keywords.
DoD: trigger AI generation for attributes.
DoD: generation is conditioned on the brand's voice guide via pgvector RAG.
DoD: user can view deterministic rule failures.
DoD: user can view vision-based image compliance issues.
DoD: rule and vision issues are formatted as unified, structured errors.
DoD: system automatically repairs field-level errors.
DoD: self-correction is bounded at max 3 retries.
DoD: system blocks gracefully when human intervention is needed.
DoD: review listings side-by-side per marketplace.
DoD: reviewer can edit fields.
DoD: approve or reject listings.
DoD: approve/reject is recorded with an audit trail.
DoD: maker-checker — creator cannot approve own listing.
DoD: publish approved listings via marketplace adapters.
DoD: publishing reports per-field success/failure.
DoD: live operational analytics.
There are 10 Non-Negotiable Architectural Invariants.
The 10 invariants are non-negotiable for the entire 45 days and beyond.
Under deadline pressure, no engineer is permitted to cut corners on these rules.
Non-Negotiable Architecture Invariants (label)
Invariant 1: AI never publishes directly.
Invariant 1: only adapters publish.
Invariant 1: adapters publish strictly after human approval.
Invariant 2: Rules Engine is deterministic code, never an LLM call.
Invariant 2: rules are the final arbiter.
Invariant 3: human approval is mandatory in MVP.
Invariant 3: zero unvetted auto-publishing in Phase 1.
Invariant 4: marketplace logic stays inside adapters.
Invariant 4: the canonical listing model never contains marketplace-specific schema structures.
Invariant 5: mandatory tenant isolation on every query.
Invariant 5: `tenant_id` scoping is enforced at the repository base class, with zero exceptions.
Invariant 6: marketplace credentials never enter LLM prompts.
Invariant 6: tokens are encrypted at rest with Cloud KMS.
Invariant 6: tokens are kept strictly isolated from AI contexts.
Invariant 7: every generation call persists an `AgentRun` record.
AgentRun record logs model.
AgentRun record logs token usage.
AgentRun record logs cost.
AgentRun record logs duration.
AgentRun record logs status.
Invariant 8 (Unified ErrorReport shape): rules engine failures return the exact same structured error contract.
Invariant 8 (Unified ErrorReport shape): vision model failures return the exact same structured error contract.
Invariant 8 (Unified ErrorReport shape): marketplace API failures return the exact same structured error contract.
Invariant 9: agent correction loops are capped at 3 attempts (max 3 retries).
Invariant 9: no infinite loops ever exist.
Invariant 10: mutations are idempotent.
Invariant 10: partial marketplace failures retry only the specific failed field, never the entire listing.
Core Operational Loop
The core operational loop is repeated to the team at every standup.
Core Execution Rhythm (label)
Core loop step 1 of 5: AI proposes.
Core loop step 2 of 5: Deterministic rules validate.
Core loop step 3 of 5: Humans approve.
Core loop step 4 of 5: Adapters execute.
Core loop step 5 of 5: Performance feeds back.
Kickoff Constraints & Solo Phase
During the first 10 days, you build solo.
Solo phase builds a razor-thin vertical slice that validates the architecture, not broad features.
Solo vertical slice covers one category.
Solo vertical slice covers one marketplace's rules.
Solo vertical slice covers one end-to-end AI call.
Days 11–14 have a 4-day slack buffer to absorb solo slippage before full-throttle scaling.

Sprint Scope Discipline Rule
The Left Column Rule (label)
A proposed feature not in the left column goes directly to the Phase 2/3 backlog.
Features do NOT get quietly slipped into Phase 1 because "it looks small."
Review the scope table at every Friday retrospective.
Explicit Non-Goals (What We Will NOT Build)
Non-goal (No Foundation Model Training): zero custom model training or fine-tuning.
Use hosted foundation models.
Hosted models sit behind a clean ModelRouter abstraction.
Non-goal: no Kubernetes — no GKE or microservice mesh overhead.
Compute runs entirely on serverless Cloud Run containers.
Non-goal: no dedicated vector database — no Pinecone, Milvus, or Weaviate.
Cloud SQL PostgreSQL with pgvector handles both relational and vector data at MVP scale.
Non-goal: no algorithm may publish to Amazon or Flipkart without an explicit human approval button click.
Non-goal: no real-time scraping of competitor listings during MVP.
Non-goal: no real-time scraping of volatile keyword trends during MVP.

The 8 agents stay on the strategic roadmap but are strictly blocked from Phase 1.
